{{Quote|Roger, roger.|Typical response of a B1 [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droid]]|audio=RogerRoger.flac|<ref name="TCW">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]]</ref>}}
'''B1-series battle droids''', also referred to as '''B1 battle droids''',  '''standard battle droids''' or '''Neimoidian Series''',<ref name="RPG-Core">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook]]''</ref> were [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] that made up the backbone of the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Trade Federation Droid Army]] and the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]]. Often called '''"Clankers"''' by [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]], they were the basis of the more advanced [[OOM-series battle droid/Legends|OOM-series battle droid]], which was considered a model of the B1 line.

B1s were perhaps the most numerous—and expendable—soldiers in [[Timeline of galactic history/Legends|galactic history]], and unlike most organic soldiers, they were capable of action in hostile environments such as underwater or in space. They were designed, for the most part, to defeat their enemies through sheer numbers, not through their ability to think (they were very vulnerable to tricks) and utilize combat skills (unlike clone troopers).

The B1 battle droid was frequently used as a soldier for the Trade Federation. As a result, B1s were present in nearly every battle involving the Trade Federation.

Early battles involving the droids required a central computer for the droids to "think" from, but this was mostly removed post–[[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]] after an attack destroyed the mainframe stationed there, resulting in all the droids on the planet being deactivated.

==Characteristics==
===Design===
{{Quote|Useless things. A greater danger to us than to Jedi.|General Grievous, the [[Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies/Legends|Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies]] of the Separatists|<ref name="ROTS novel">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref>}}
B1 battle droids stood 1.93 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall and were [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] in form.<ref name="SWE" /><ref name="Databank" /> Their long, elongated heads atop tall, slender necks were designed in imitation of their builders at [[Baktoid Combat Automata/Legends|Baktoid's]] [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosian]] foundries.<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> Fearful<ref name="TNEGTD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] crewers were known to spread the rumor that B1 [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]]' heads were designed to imitate the shape of a [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian's]]<ref name="EGW" /> withered skull after death,<ref name="Episode I: The Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> and many species found the B1's appearance disturbing.<ref name="EGW" /> They were powered by rechargeable batteries, with each charge allowing them to operate for approximately two [[Standard day/Legends|days]].<ref name="pathways">{{CWACite|8|Pathways}}</ref>

[[File:B1schematic-SWBC13.png|thumb|left|350px|B1 battle droid schematics]]
Some B1 units, designated the [[OOM-series battle droid/Legends|OOM-series]], were given expanded programming and color-coded according to function, such as commander or security.<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide">''[[Arms & Equipment Guide]]''</ref> Some were painted with different colors to blend into a certain environment, such as the reddish-colored B1 droids manufactured on Geonosis.<ref name="Databank" /> B1s were usually slaved to a central control mainframe located on a remote [[Starship/Legends|starship]] or another well-defended facility. However, this could lead to massive failure if the central control mainframe was destroyed, such as during the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]], in which [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] destroyed the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|Droid Control Ship]].<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" /> The monumental defeat at [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] spurred interest in independent battle droids, and this technique gained ground following the battle and during the Clone Wars.

[[File:Beetledroid.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A beetle-mounted B1 droid armed with a flamethrower]]
The electromagnets that kept their limbs attached could malfunction. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] learned to aim at the hips, torsos, and arm joints of the B1s to quickly destroy them. But a head shot was the only decisive way to disable a droid. They didn't need arms, legs or even bodies to pass intel to central command.

B1s were designed for cheap mass-production. As a result, they were very flimsy and vulnerable but were capable of swarming an enemy with their hugely superior numbers. Other models, like the [[Droideka/Legends|droideka]], [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|B2 super battle droid]], [[B2 grapple droid/Legends|grapple droid]], and [[B1-A air battle droid]], were more expensive and as a result less widely used but better soldiers.

Battle droids used [[E-5 blaster rifle/Legends|E-5 blaster rifles]], [[SE-14 blaster pistol]]s, and [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonators]] in combat.<ref name="Battlefront II" /> They spoke in a high-pitched monotone. The voice varied between units around the time of the Battle of Naboo, and at some point during the Clone Wars their voices were uniformly changed to a more high-pitched version.<ref name="TCW" />

===Performance===
{{Quote|Ouch time.|[[Roos Tarpals/Legends|Roos Tarpals]], commenting on the battle droids' before the Battle of Grassy Plains|<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" />}}
[[File:Battle_Droid_SWD_2018_Season_2_OP_Elite_Prize_Card.png|thumb|right|250px|B1 battle droids deploy during the Battle of Naboo.]]

B1 droids employed unsophisticated tactics in battle. Massed parade ranks or simple swarms were used, and they didn't often display a concept of cover.<ref name="Star Wars: Clone Wars">''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]''</ref> During the Clone Wars, however, there was the inevitable development of wartime, and B1 programming began to show some improvement. Nevertheless, their in-battle reactions were often slow, and such initiative as was shown was slight.<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" /> [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], the commander of the droid army, hated battle droids for their weakness in comparison to the Republic's clone troopers.

Although they appeared to be weak, B1s were able to take down an enemy in hand-to-hand combat as seen in the Battle of Grassy Plains where battle droids were able to take [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] soldiers one-on-one.<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" />

Although the earlier generations were entirely dependent on [[Central Control Computer/Legends|Central Control Computers]], post-Naboo models were retrofitted with cognitive models that allowed independent thought, and featured a greater degree of independence and personality.<ref name="Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith">{{Film|III}}</ref> However, labored with more and more specialized roles that pushed the limits of their programming, many older droids developed personality quirks and a tendency to excessively comment on their situations in an attempt to handle the data overflow that had strained their inadequate logic modules.<ref name="SW:TCWCE" /><ref name="TOEG">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars – The Official Episode Guide: Season 1]]''</ref>

==History==
B1s were used by a variety of governments and armed forces. Even smugglers were known to use them, but in smaller amounts compared to the galactic armies of the [[Commerce Guild/Legends|commerce guilds]].<ref name="TCW" />

===Invasion of Naboo===
[[File:STAP_TPM.png|thumb|left|200px|A B1 piloting a [[Single Trooper Aerial Platform/Legends|Single Trooper Aerial Platform]] on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].]]
B1 battle droids were used extensively during the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] by Viceroy [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]]. Although the droids were statistically flimsy, with overwhelming numbers they were able to subdue the Naboo and maintain surface control of the planet. The Trade Federation invasion force which held Naboo until the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]] was mostly composed of B1s, droidekas and other mechanized vehicles such as [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|AATs]], [[Multi-Troop Transport/Legends|MTTs]], [[Single Trooper Aerial Platform/Legends|STAPs]], and [[Platoon Attack Craft/Legends|PACs]].

Upon their arrival to the Trade Federation blockade of the planet, [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] Knights [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] highlighted weaknesses of the droids. These technical shortcomings, including a slow reaction time, weapon inaccuracy, and straight-forward tactics, stemmed from the nature of the Trade Federation quantity-over-quality production of B1s.

The "primitive" [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]] and the bulk of the Trade Federation invasion force ultimately fought openly in the Battle of Grassy Plains. Although the uneven nature of the terrain and innovative tactics of the Gungans initially posed a problem, the overwhelming supply of B1s and other machines on the battlefield proved to be the trump card.

The turning point and saving grace of the Battle of Naboo proved to be the destruction of the [[Vuutun Palaa/Legends|Droid Control Ship]] by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]]. After the [[Central Control Computer/Legends|Central Control Computer]] of the droid army was destroyed, all mechanized units on the Grassy Plains reset and became inanimate, harmless constructions.<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" />

===Post-Naboo===
[[File:Battle_Droids_Geonosis.png|thumb|right|250px|B1 battle droids in action during the Battle of Geonosis.]]
Upon the closure of the Naboo crisis, the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] passed legislation that prohibited the Trade Federation's use of droid armies and the development of military hardware. The Trade Federation, however, relocated its military research and production centers to extra-Republican territories, like [[Geonosis droid factories/Legends|Geonosis]].

During this time, the Trade Federation began to recuperate from Republic ordinance and the incredible financial loss from the Naboo fiasco. Existing models of battle droids were improved, and new generations of soldiers were developed, such as the [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|Super Battle Droid]].<ref name="EGW" />

The B1s, however, were retooled and refitted. Learning from the destruction of the Droid Control Ship above Naboo, the Trade Federation upgraded B1s with on-board independent intelligence centers that could operate without a master signal.<ref name="Databank" /> The spherical centers of the Droid Control Ships were also redesigned to operate on land, which proved to be easier to defend. These newly retrofitted droids were able to be programmed with new tasks, and B1s became [[Warship/Legends|warship]] crewers, [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]], [[Gunner/Legends|gunners]], and [[Firefighter droid/Legends|emergency responders]].<ref name="EGW" /> However, these tasks pushed the B1s to the limits of their capabilities, and they proved to be rather poor in specialized roles. The entry of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] into the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] did not improve unit quality, as the Neimoidians refused to spend more money on improving their droids and the [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]] reserved its more powerful cognitive modules for newer, ever-more deadly war droids.<ref name="EGW" />

[[File:B1_battle_droid_malfunction_EGTW.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A malfunction of a B1 battle droid]]
These problems would be compounded as the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] went on. Maintenance became exceedingly problematic: diagnostics and memory defragmentation routines tended to erase retrofitted specialty programming, so they were frequently skipped. Cognitive modules gradually suffered data corruption and system errors, leading to shutdowns or behavioral anomalies. To the annoyance of Separatist commanders, B1s became "chatty," offering running commentaries on their situations as their modules struggled to process data overflows.<ref name="EGW" />

Following the invasion of Naboo, the [[Ultragungans]] kept a large amount of B1 battle droids as spoils of war.<ref name="SWG:ORDMTGBD" />

===Battle of Geonosis===
[[File:Rust_brown_B1_battle_droid.png|thumb|right|250px|A rust brown B1, the coloration seen at the Battle of Geonosis]]
In 22 BBY, Jedi Knight Obi-Wan Kenobi, whilst tracking [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] to Geonosis, discovered the [[Geonosis droid factories/Legends|droid foundry]] there and contacted the Jedi Council before being convicted for espionage. His apprentice Anakin Skywalker and Padmé Amidala tracked him but were also captured. All three were sentenced to be executed. However, when the three escaped their chains and the arena beasts, and a team of two hundred Jedi [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|arrived]], B1s, alongside new B2 super battle droids, entered the arena to stop the Jedi. Many droids were destroyed, but the rest overwhelmed the Jedi through sheer numbers and herded the surviving twenty into the center of the arena. However, clone troopers arrived and rescued the Jedi, and a huge battle ignited outside.

B1s fought clone troopers and Jedi alongside other Separatist droids. However, the clones proved superior, and the battle was won for the Republic. However, many droids escaped the planet aboard Trade Federation core ships, Techno Union ''Hardcell''-class transports, and other ships. The Clone Wars had just begun.

===Clone Wars===
{{Quote|You expect victory over Jedi, but all you give me to fight them is battle droids!|General Grievous, to Count Dooku|<ref name="Lair of Grievous">{{TCW|Lair of Grievous}}</ref>}}
[[File:B1s_Christophsis.png|thumb|left|250px|B1 battle droids during the [[Battle of Christophsis/Legends|Battle of Christophsis]].]]
After the Trade Federation joined the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], they became a majority of the Separatist Droid Army. B1s would be the Confederacy's most common soldiers, with alleged quintillions churned out on countless CIS factory worlds.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> Some Confederate commanders such as [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] often grew frustrated at the droids, even at times considering them "useless."<ref name="ROTS novel" /> The battle droids earned the nickname by clone troopers of "clankers."<ref name="RC">''[[Republic Commando: Hard Contact]]''</ref>

B1 battle droids would often serve on board [[Starship/Legends|starships]] and [[Battleship/Legends|battleships]]. They would man [[Autoturret/Legends|turrets]], work [[Computer/Legends|computer]] consoles, drive warships, and serve as security aboard the vessel.<ref name="destroy malevolence">{{TCW|Destroy Malevolence|Destroy ''Malevolence''}}</ref>

They participated in many battles including, but not limited to, the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|First Battle of Geonosis]], [[Battle of Muunilinst/Legends|Battle of Muunilinst]],<ref name="Battlefront II" /> [[Siege of Cato Neimoidia|Battle of Cato Neimoidia]],<ref name="LOE">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref> [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]], and [[Battle of Kashyyyk/Legends|Battle of Kashyyyk]].<ref name="Battlefront II" />' Despite their notable combat ineffectiveness, B1 Battle Droids did successfully [[Battle of Dathomir/Legends|eradicate]] the Nightsisters clan on Dathomir.<ref name="Massacre">{{TCW|Massacre}}</ref> Training models were even used on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] for the practice tests of [[Clone cadet/Legends|Clone cadets]].

[[File:Battle_Droids_Working.png|thumb|right|250px|B1 battle droids working computer consoles on board ''Malevolence''.]]
During the Clone Wars, ARC [[Prudii Skirata]] spoke to and managed to "convince" an important Separatist metallurgist to give him vital clues on the metallurgic structure of droids. By adding 5% extra [[carvanium]] to the droids via the main factory computer at [[Olanet]], these droids crumbled when hit with any weapon. The sabotage acts were so successful that the kill ratio for clone troopers was raised from 20 droids per clone to 50 droids per clone during the first year of the Clone Wars.<ref name="Odds">{{InsiderCite|87|Odds}}</ref>

The Separatists eventually plotted to replace the B1 with an [[updated battle droid]] model, the designs of which were stored on a [[Datachip/Legends|datachip]] in an [[Unidentified Separatist factory|factory]]. During a Republic [[Raid on a Separatist factory|raid]], a [[Unidentified B1 battle droid (Separatist factory)|single B1 droid]] ensured the plans were recovered to Dooku, but the B1 disobeyed his masters by destroying the chip after learning of its purpose, ensuring his B1 brethren would not be reduced to spare parts.<ref name="Update comic">{{TCWComicCite|6.53|Update}}</ref> Following the execution of the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]] by [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious's]] new [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], most, if not all, of the B1s were de-activated. However, some would be re-activated to serve in the various [[Separatist holdouts/Legends|Confederate Remnants]], such as the one controlled by [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosian]] [[Gizor Dellso]].<ref name="Battlefront II" />

===Post–Clone Wars===
{{Quote|Send a message to the ships of the Trade Federation: All droid units must shut down immediately.|[[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], to [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]|<ref name="Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith" />}}
Soon after Order 66, surviving Jedi [[Olee Starstone]] and [[Roan Shryne]] fled to [[Jaguada/Legends|Jaguada]], a former Separatist base. Attempting to contact Jedi on Coruscant, they accidentally activated the droid guards. Vader discovered their position and sent troops from the planet to destroy them. The Jedi used the activated droids to serve as a rear-guard against the troopers.<ref name="DL:TRODV">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref>

During the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]], some B1s were reactivated and reprogrammed for use as security droids.<ref name="Against the Empire">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Against the Empire]]''</ref> In addition, some were used by Darth Vader to have [[Falco Sang]] undergo various intense trials. He initially had the droids armed with stun blasters, although Sang saw through the ruse and ceased either evading the attacks or even shooting back and also attempted escape twice. Upon learning this, Vader ordered the staff to replace the stinger blasters with live blasters, also giving strict orders to have them wound him rather than kill him.<ref name="FC1" />

[[File:B1AdvancedBattleDroid.jpg|thumb|left|150px|A variant of the B1 often encountered by [[Delta Squad/Legends|Delta Squad]]]]
At some point before [[12 BBY/Legends|12 BBY]], [[Gizor Dellso]] reactivated a droid army on [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]]. Shortly after this, the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] quickly destroyed the army and Dellso in the [[Battle of Mustafar (Imperial Period)|Battle of Mustafar]].

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], B1s left over from the Clone Wars were discovered on Geonosis by [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] pilot [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] after crash landing in his [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]]. Several [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] that had landed on the planet in [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pods]] managed to destroy many droids by using [[E-Web heavy repeating blaster/Legends|E-web blasters]], but they ultimately fell to the battle droids' overwhelming blaster fire.<ref name="Rogue Squadron III">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref>

Other B1s that weren't deactivated were used in the [[Death Watch bunker]], known crash sites on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], Separatist holdouts, [[Stonewall Labs]] and [[Borvo's Vault]] on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], and even on [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]].<ref name="SWG:AED" /> [[Osaji Uhares]] repaired some and used them as his bodyguards on [[Centares/Legends|Centares]].<ref name="Triplet Threat">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20040122threat|text=Triplet Threat|int=Triplet Threat}}</ref>

Some of these droids were used by [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] pirates in the [[Death Watch bunker]].<ref name="SWG:AED" /> The [[Jawa/Legends|Jawa]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Wittin/Legends|Wittin]] used one on a [[Single Trooper Aerial Platform/Legends|Single Trooper Aerial Platform]] to compete in [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure's]] demolition games.<ref name="Demolitions">''[[Star Wars: Demolition]]''</ref>

The [[IG-97 battle droid|IG-97]] droid bore a close resemblance to the original B1 battle droid, although being developed by [[Holowan Mechanicals/Legends|Holowan Mechanicals]] after plans by [[Phlut Design Systems/Legends|Phlut Design Systems]] who had been working for the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]].

===Impact on galactic society===
[[Action figure|Toy versions]] of the B1 battle droid were manufactured. [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett's]] cloned son [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] had some during his youth on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]].<ref name="Star Wars: Jango Fett">[[Star Wars: Jango Fett (one-shot)|''Star Wars: Jango Fett'']]</ref>

The Confederacy's extensive use of B1s contributed to the general distrust of droids in galactic society during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]].<ref name="EGW" />

==Behind the scenes==
B1 battle droids first appeared in [[1999]] with the release of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']]. ''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary|Star Wars Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]'' provides a key to color coding in relation to their rank and function, and a table to decipher their numerical digits.

The earliest designs of the battle droid were clearly inspired by the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] of the [[original trilogy]], suggesting the evolution of large-scale combat in the ''Star Wars'' galaxy. The finished droid's proportions are reminiscent of African sculpture. Early design had towering droids twice the height of humans, but subsequent iterations brought their height down to human size.<ref name="Databank" />

The "B1" designation originated with the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'', to differentiate the battle droid from other models introduced in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], and the name was retroactively applied to its earlier appearances. Prior to this, the ''Roleplaying Game'' had once identified it as the "Nemoidian Series."

The video games ''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron]]'' and ''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Elite Squadron]]'' feature the labels "Battledroid Mk II" and "Battledroid Mk III" in the personalization editor, though the customization was up to the player.
